notizie.titolo: Vulnerabilità critica in PHP scoperta con l'ausilio dell'AI
notizie.riassunto: Una grave vulnerabilità nel linguaggio PHP è stata individuata tramite modelli di intelligenza artificiale, spingendo gli sviluppatori a rilasciare patch urgenti per milioni di siti web.

a162.titolo: PHP rilascia patch per le vulnerabilità scoperte da GPT-5.6 Sol
a162.testo: Il PHP Group ha rilasciato le patch per le due gravi vulnerabilità, denominate PHP2Shell, che permettono l’esecuzione di codice remoto senza autenticazione. Gli utenti devono quindi installare immediatamente le ultime versioni del popolare linguaggio di programmazione. OpenAI ha svelato che le vulnerabilità sono state trovate con l’aiuto del modello GPT-5.6 Sol. PHP2Shell interessa il 70% dei siti mondiali Le due vulnerabilità, identificate con CVE-2026-109618 e CVE-2026-109619, sono state scoperte all’inizio di agosto dai ricercatori di Calif. I cybercriminali potrebbero eseguire codice arbitrario sui server senza autenticazione. Le conseguenze sarebbero disastrose, in quanto PHP viene utilizzato da oltre il 70% dei siti mondiali, inclusi quelli basati su noti CMS (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla). Per l’analisi del problema di sicurezza e la successiva risoluzione c’è stata una stretta collaborazione tra diverse aziende e organizzazioni, tra cui PHP Foundation, Calif, OpenAI, Wiz e Cloudflare. Calif e PHP Foundation partecipano all’iniziativa Patch the Planet di OpenAI. L’azienda californiana spiega che Calif ha scoperto le vulnerabilità con l’aiuto del modello GPT-5.6 Sol. PHP Foundation sottolinea che le patch dovevano essere rilasciate il 22 ottobre, ma Chainguard non ha rispettato l’embargo, quindi la distribuzione è stata anticipata ad oggi. Le due vulnerabilità sono presenti a partire da PHP 5.4, ma le versioni precedenti alla 8.1 non ricevono più aggiornamenti. Le patch sono stati incluse in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 e 8.2.35. Gli utenti e gli amministratori IT devono pertanto installare con urgenza le ultime versioni. a141.titolo: Gemini's Personal Intelligence is coming to cars
a141.testo: Google kicked off 2026 with the addition of Personal Intelligence to Gemini, allowing its AI to pull in more of your data to formulate answers. It started as a paid feature but eventually came to all Gemini users. However, this feature wasn’t available in the car until now. Google is rolling out Personal Intelligence to Android Auto and Google Built-in, and it is still, thankfully, an optional feature. As Google points out, a generative AI’s outputs are better “when it knows the world and knows you,” which is correct in an uncomfortable sort of way. The more context you can provide to a model, the better the output will be at the end of the token shuffle. Since Google has so much of your data already, it sees Personal Intelligence as a differentiator versus other AI systems. You don’t have to provide the AI context because it already has it from apps like Gmail and Calendar. Personal Intelligence is beginning its rollout in Android Auto today, and it will come to vehicles with Google built-in in the next few months. As an aside, “Google built-in” is questionable branding, but it refers to cars that run Google software in the infotainment system rather than projecting an interface from your phone. Very few vehicles have Google built-in, but Google often releases new car features on them first. This time, it’s the other way around. Google says Personal Intelligence is a natural fit for the car, allowing you to focus on the road instead of providing detailed instructions to your digital assistant. For example, you can say “take me to my doctor’s appointment,” and Gemini can get that data from your connected calendar. It can also leverage visual analysis to find locations in your photos to begin navigation.

Every apartment block, bus lane and factory goes through hearings, reviews, objections, lawsuits and appeals. The economy underneath is real. The neighbors are not always rational. a129.titolo: PHP Armageddon: OpenAI, Google’s Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet
a129.testo: The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out an alarming warning on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation. PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet; by some accounts, that’s more than 33 million sites. It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress. The NSA warned that these holes are so severe that if a website can’t be patched immediately, it should be pulled off the web until it can be. The holes allow attackers to infiltrate the server’s file system or a database that may be used by the web app. Interestingly, these holes have been tucked away in all versions of PHP since version 5, which was released in 2004. Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12. So how did two such ubiquitous, decades-old flaws that affect nearly every website on the internet suddenly come to light? AI, naturally, particularly via OpenAI and Google’s Wiz. Security testing company Calif was engaged in OpenAI’s “Patch the Planet” initiative to find flaws in open source software. Using GPT‑5.6 Sol, it found one of the flaws, OpenAI disclosed in a blog post. Separately, the Wiz team also used AI, namely its Wiz Atlas security AI agent, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol to find multiple vulnerabilities in PHP. Both OpenAI and Wiz followed responsible security research practices and worked with PHP on patches before publicly disclosing the flaws.
